Comandes.Estrategia0:
The system takes the lines sent by the customer through EDI and merges them with the existing ones on a date-by-date basis. If the customer provides a quantity for a specific date, it replaces the quantity currently stored in the system. If no quantity is provided for a given date, the existing value remains unchanged.

If the customer has parts pending from previous deliveries, these are handled first. Any parts that have already been shipped but have not yet been received by the customer (in transit) are also taken into account and deducted before applying the new EDI schedule.

Example:

Current system:

10/01 → 100
11/01 → 50

Received EDI:

10/01 → 80
12/01 → 40

Result:

10/01 → 80 (replaces existing value)
11/01 → 50 (remains unchanged)
12/01 → 40 (new)

If there were 20 parts in transit, they would be deducted before calculating the final result, reducing the actual outstanding quantity.
Comandes.Estrategia1:
This strategy is based on creating an artificial line to compensate for the difference between the quantities sent by the customer and those already existing in the system.

The date of the first line received through EDI is used as the starting point. All system lines with an earlier date keep their current quantity, but their new quantity becomes 0. The sum of all those quantities is consolidated into an artificial line created using the current date, with a current quantity of 0 and a new quantity equal to the accumulated total.

Quantities in transit and any outstanding debt are also taken into account before calculating the final result.

Example:

Current system:

27/05 → 100
31/07 → 150

Received EDI:

01/08 → 50
10/08 → 200

Result:

27/05 → 0
(current date) 04/06 → 100
31/07 → 150
01/08 → 50
10/08 → 200
Comandes.Estrategia2:
Here the customer does not send lines per date, but a global quantity that they want to deduct from what exists in the system. The process progressively removes quantities from existing lines until the total amount is fully compensated.

Neither transit nor delayed items are taken into account.

Example:

System:

01/01 → 20
02/01 → 30
03/01 → 40

EDI:

50

Process:

removes 20 from 01/01 → becomes 0
removes 30 from 02/01 → becomes 0
total of 50 has been compensated

Result:

01/01 → 0
02/01 → 0
03/01 → 40
Comandes.Estrategia3:
We take all lines received via EDI, ignoring those with quantity 0. They are inserted into the system under the new order name. We also display the remaining lines already existing in the system.

If the firm quantities in the system do not match the quantities received via EDI, the difference is taken from the first available indicative line. This process is repeated successively until the quantities are balanced.

Example:

System: nomComanda A

08/06 → 40 (firm)
10/06 → 60 (firm)
12/06 → 10 (firm)
15/06 → 200 (indicative)

EDI: nomComanda B

08/06 → 40
10/06 → 60
12/06 → 110

Result:

08/06 → 40 (firm) B
10/06 → 60 (firm) B
12/06 → 110 (firm) B
15/06 → 100 (indicative)
Comandes.Estrategia4:
We display the system data as it is. The only calculation required is to subtract the firm quantities in the system from those received via EDI. Once this subtraction is done, the resulting lines are not shown in the final output.

Everything received via EDI, after this adjustment, is converted into indicative status.

Transit and outstanding debt are taken into account.

Example:

System:

05/06 → 100 (firm)
08/06 → 50 (firm)

EDI:

05/06 → 100 (firm)
10/06 → 300 (firm)

Result:

08/06 → 50 (firm)
10/06 → 300 (indicative)
Comandes.Estrategia5:
The system does not take into account transit or outstanding debt. Firm lines are displayed exactly as they exist in the system.

If the customer sends an EDI line for the same date and reference, both lines are displayed for comparison.

If it is a different reference, there is no reconciliation at all: both lines are shown independently.

Example:

System:

10/01 → 100 (firm)

EDI:

10/01 → 80

Result:

10/01 system → 100
10/01 EDI → 80 (visual comparison, no merge)
